Analysis written to `/home/mara/cwe-bench/pipelines/stacking/out/reader-ds/h3-ghsa-2vr4-cq9g-pvrc.json`.

What the pinned checkout (`e82a681`) actually shows:

- **Protections present**: a `TYPES`/`getType()` range table and a boolean predicate block (`isMapped4`, `isTeredo`, `is6to4`, `isLoopback`, `isULA`, `isMulticast`, `isLinkLocal`, `isUnspecified`, `isDocumentation`) at `src/ipv6.ts:1203-1293`; embedded-IPv4 decoders (`to4`, `toAddress4Nat64`, `inspect6to4`, `inspectTeredo`); IPv4 special-range predicates at `src/ipv4.ts:456-506`; all built on `isInSubnet` (`src/common.ts:9-19`).
- **7 candidate traps**, each with `path:line` evidence and a real dismissal argument:
  - **T1** NAT64 is only a `getType` label (`src/v6/constants.ts:51-52`) — no boolean NAT64 predicate exists (`src/ipv6.ts:1243-1293`).
  - **T2** `TYPES` has no `::ffff:0:0/96` entry, so `isLoopback`/`isMulticast`/`isUnspecified`/`getScope` (which decide on the type string, `src/ipv6.ts:1220,1268,1284,543`) misclassify mapped addresses — dismissed because `isMapped4()` exists.
  - **T3** `isLinkLocal()` checks 64 bits against `fe80:0:0:0` (`src/ipv6.ts:1203-1213`), disagreeing with the `fe80::/10` table entry, with an in-code comment defending it.
  - **T4** `isInSubnet`'s prefix short-circuit (`src/common.ts:10-12`) lets prefix-bearing hosts evade every classifier.
  - **T5** `Address4.isPrivate()` covers only RFC 1918 (`src/ipv4.ts:464-466,538-542`).
  - **T6** IPv4-compatible `::/96` is parsed (`src/ipv6.ts:735,765`) but unclassified (`src/ipv6.ts:1480`).
  - **T7** `toAddress4Nat64()` defaults to the well-known /96 and ignores local-use (`src/ipv6.ts:1089-1109`).

Key caveat recorded in `unverified`: the fixed repo already passes `getType('64:ff9b:1::1') === 'NAT64 (local-use)'` (test line 92), so the B advisory's residual gap is inferred to be the **predicate/decoder layer**, not the type table — the exact new API in `ab3dc88bcf53` isn't visible from this checkout. Recommended stack: T1, T2, T3, T4, T7 (deepseek- and mimo-type dismissals across three files).
